name: Queenstown Airport
before:
Queenstown's airport, at Frankton, and fourth busiest in New Zealand with 2.7 million passengers in 2025. For a resort town that is remarkable traffic.

It is known for two things. The first is the approach, which is genuinely demanding: high terrain close in and housing near the field. The second is the scenery on the way down, which clients tend to remember.

The terminal is a single level building with nine gates handling both domestic and international flights, and there are no jet bridges, so every boarding is on foot. A 2015 expansion of the international departures area built a mezzanine so jet bridges could be added later.

Air New Zealand and Jetstar fly domestically to Auckland, Wellington and Christchurch, and the trans-Tasman routes to Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane and the Gold Coast are flown by Air New Zealand, Jetstar, Qantas and Virgin Australia. Sightseeing flights to Milford Sound and Aoraki Mount Cook also leave from here.

Auckland Airport has held a 24.99 per cent stake since 2010.
after:
Queenstown's airport at Frankton is New Zealand's fourth busiest. The airport says it handled a record 2.82 million passengers in the year to June 2026. For a resort town that is remarkable traffic.

The approach is demanding, with high terrain close in and housing near the field. Clients tend to remember the scenery on the way down.

The airport's single-level terminal has nine gates and handles domestic and international flights. There are no jet bridges: passengers walk between aircraft and terminal. A 2015 expansion of the international terminal added a mezzanine to allow for jet bridges later.

Between them, Air New Zealand, Jetstar, Qantas and Virgin Australia fly to Auckland, Wellington and Christchurch and across the Tasman to Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane and the Gold Coast. Sightseeing flights to Milford Sound and Aoraki Mount Cook also leave from here.

Auckland Airport has held a 24.99 per cent stake since 2010.

claims.claim: the airport says it handled a record 2.82 million passengers in the year to June 2026
claims.inAfter: The airport says it handled a record 2.82 million passengers in the year to June 2026.
claims.note: Was '2.7 million passengers in 2025'. Wikipedia's calendar-2025 figure (2,717,113, from Auckland Airport's monthly traffic updates) could not be checked against a second organisation: Auckland Airport's corporate site and NZX both refused the link lister (403) and were not tried again, and the Otago Daily Times' Queenstown page carried no airport story. The airport's own figure for the financial year to 30 June 2026 is newer, so it replaces the calendar figure (a passenger total for a passenger total), attributed to the airport. Its 'passenger movements' count arriving and departing passengers together, the usual airport total. Its June release had forecast about 2.8 million.

claims.claim: the approach is demanding, with high terrain close in and housing near the field
claims.inAfter: The approach is demanding, with high terrain close in and housing near the field.
claims.note: 'Genuinely demanding' is now 'demanding', the Civil Aviation Authority's word. Its booklet In, out, and around Queenstown (revised September 2024, hosted on the airport's operations page) is written for visiting pilots, but its introduction is about flying into the aerodrome as a whole. The housing: the booklet tells pilots to avoid overflying residential areas, 'in particular over Frankton Arm and the town', and the airport's history says homes and businesses have grown up around it at Frankton.
